questions: Should the function raise an error if the specified column contains non-numeric data, or should it attempt to fit a normal distribution anyway (which would likely fail or produce nonsense)?
If the column contains NaN values, should they be silently dropped, cause an error, or be handled in some other way?
Should the function close or clear the current matplotlib figure before creating the plot, or should it plot on the current axes if they exist?
Is the 'density' parameter intended to match the matplotlib.hist 'density' parameter exactly (i.e., normalizing area to 1) or should it have a custom interpretation?
Should the function set any specific limits (xlim, ylim) beyond those automatically determined by matplotlib?
If the column name contains special characters (e.g., spaces, quotes), should the title be escaped or formatted differently?
Should the function return the Axes object immediately after plotting, or should it also call plt.show() or similar?
Is the seed parameter intended to affect only numpy random operations, or also any other potential randomness (e.g., from pandas or matplotlib)?
